## For information - navigating Databricks:

:::

## Task 1 

::: callout-important
## Folder location

:::

-   Go to the [workshop repository page](https://dfe-gov-uk.visualstudio.com/official-statistics-production/_git/git_refresher_workshop).

-   Click the “Clone” button and copy the URL (HTTPS link).

![](images/copy_https.png)

-   Navigate to the folder on your device where you want to clone the repo. Right-click in the directory and select “Git Bash Here”.
    -   If you don't have a folder created outside OneDrive, then create one.

![](images/clone_gitbash_location.png)

-   In the Git Bash window that opens, use the `git clone` command followed by the URL you copied from GitHub. For this repo, we would enter:

```{r,eval=FALSE}

git clone https://dfe-gov-uk.visualstudio.com/skills-policy-analysis/_git/git_refresher_workshop

```

::: callout-warning
## Copying and pasting

You will need to right-click to paste, as the keyboard shortcut will not work in Git Bash and then press enter.
:::

## Task 2 - Create a branch

-   Click on Branches under repos to open the Branches view.

![](images/navigate_to_repo.png){width="465"}

-   Click on the New branch button.

:::{.callout-tip}

## Only one person should do this - Create a base branch for your group

One of you must do this step before carrying on. 

One person in your group needs to create a branch called `workshop_<your_group_number>` and replace `<your_group_number>` with the number your group was assigned. Make sure `master` is the base branch. Only ONE person from your group needs to do this. 
:::

-   Enter `read_in_data_<your_group_number>` for your new branch and make sure `workshop_<your_group_number>` is the base branch.
-   Click on the Create button to create your new branch.

![](images/create_branch.png){width="465"}

## Task 3 - Pulling changes and switching branches

### Task 3a - Pulling changes

-   Open the R Project file called `git_refresher_workshop.Rproj` in RStudio if you haven't already.

-   In the top-right corner of RStudio, find the Git pane.

    -   If you don't see it, go to Tools \> Version Control \> Project Setup and ensure Git is enabled.
    
-   Click on the Pull button (downwards arrow) in the Git pane.

    -   This will fetch changes from the remote repository and update your local one. 

![](images/pull_r.png)
